territory: Cross-cutting lens: every date/time computation and render across the UTC (server) / IST (members) seam — day-boundary math, server-rendered date formatting, relative-time helpers and hydration, email budget window, catchup cadence, admin analytics bucketing, MetricSnapshot, Visit/session math, feedSeenAt, token expiry displays

findings.title: Admin analytics rhythm heatmap applies AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata' in the wrong direction, shifting every hour bucket by -11 hours
findings.expected: loadRhythm() buckets visits into IST hour-of-day and weekday, so the 8pm IST evening rush shows at hour 20; the code comment states this is the whole point: "IST, not UTC ... a UTC heatmap would put the evening rush at 2pm and make the whole thing meaningless."
findings.actual: Every bucket is shifted -11 hours (and DOW shifts across the boundary). A visit at 20:00 IST is stored as naive 14:30 (UTC wall time, since Visit.endedAt is TIMESTAMP(3) without time zone); `"endedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata'` INTERPRETS that naive 14:30 as IST wall time, producing the instant 09:00 UTC; EXTRACT(HOUR FROM timestamptz) then converts using the session TimeZone (UTC on Supabase, node-postgres never sets one), yielding hour 9. The 5:30 offset is applied twice in the wrong direction instead of once forward. The heatmap and its "peak" tile are systematically wrong yet look plausible, which is worse than obviously broken: the owner built this to decide when the community is awake.
findings.evidence: src/lib/admin-analytics.ts:583-585: `SELECT EXTRACT(DOW  FROM "endedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::int AS dow, EXTRACT(HOUR FROM "endedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::int AS hour`. The column is naive: prisma/migrations-manual/2026-08-19-presence.sql:18: `"endedAt"   TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` — and Prisma writes UTC wall-time into naive columns (bugs.md item 6 documents the app's columns are `timestamp without time zone`). Postgres semantics: naive AT TIME ZONE zone = "interpret this wall time as being IN zone, return timestamptz"; EXTRACT on a timestamptz renders in the session TimeZone first. So stored 14:30 (true instant 14:30 UTC = 20:00 IST) → interpreted as 14:30 IST → 09:00 UTC instant → EXTRACT under UTC session = 9. Correct value is 20; the correct expression needs the naive value anchored to UTC first.
findings.fixDirection: Change both expressions to double conversion: `EXTRACT(DOW FROM ("endedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')` (same for HOUR). The inner AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' turns the naive UTC wall time into a real timestamptz; the outer one converts it to IST wall time (a naive value, on which EXTRACT is session-independent).
findings.gateOrTest: A node --test unit in the src/lib/*.test.mjs style cannot run SQL; instead pin it with a read-only SQL assertion in a script test or add a JS-side sanity check: insert-free — SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM (TIMESTAMP '2026-08-21 14:30:00' AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') must be 20. At minimum, a comment-pinned example in loadRhythm and a one-off verification query in the fix session.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: run `SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM TIMESTAMP '2026-08-21 14:30:00' AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') AT TIME ZONE ...` — concretely, `SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM (TIMESTAMP '2026-08-21 14:30:00') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') AS wrong, EXTRACT(HOUR FROM ((TIMESTAMP '2026-08-21 14:30:00') AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') AS right;` via a read-only session — expect wrong=9, right=20. No table access needed.

findings.title: Catch-ups Round reader renders 'Published {date}' and 'Next Round opens {date}' in server UTC, one day early for late-night IST times
findings.expected: A Round published at 00:20 IST on 22 Aug reads "Published 22 August 2026"; "Next Round opens 5 September" names the IST calendar day members will actually find it open.
findings.actual: Both components are server components (no "use client"; rendered by the server page catchups/round/[editionId]/page.tsx) and call toLocaleDateString without a timeZone, so they format in the server's UTC zone. Any publishedAt/nextOpensAt instant falling 18:30-24:00 UTC (00:00-05:30 IST, i.e. any round auto-published past midnight India time — transitions fire lazily on page views, so late-night publishes are common) renders the previous day. Worst is footer-tease: nextOpensAt = publishedAt + cadence gap; "Next Round opens 4 September" for a round that opens 02:00 IST Sep 5 sends members to check on the 4th and find nothing.
findings.evidence: masthead.tsx:49-55: `const dateLabel = publishedAt ? new Date(publishedAt).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" }) : null;` — no timeZone. footer-tease.tsx:24-31: `showNextOpens && nextOpensAt ? new Date(nextOpensAt).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", {...})` — no timeZone. Neither file carries "use client"; both are imported only by the server page (grep: catchups/round/[editionId]/page.tsx). Server runs UTC on Vercel, so toLocaleDateString uses the UTC calendar day.
findings.fixDirection: Add `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"` to both toLocaleDateString option objects (the site's editorial day is the Valley's day). Consider routing both through a single shared IST-pinned formatter (see the utils.ts finding) so no future surface repeats this.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test in node --test style: with TZ=UTC (CI default), format new Date('2026-08-21T19:30:00Z') and assert '22 August 2026', not '21 August 2026'. Runs under the existing npm run check test harness if the formatter moves into src/lib/utils.ts.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof would need a round whose publishedAt sits in the 18:30-24:00 UTC window; equivalent one-liner: `TZ=UTC node -e "console.log(new Date('2026-08-21T19:30:00Z').toLocaleDateString('en-GB',{day:'numeric',month:'long',year:'numeric'}))"` prints 21 August where IST says 22).

findings.actual: Server component (no "use client", imported by the server page catchups/page.tsx) formats publishedAt without a timeZone → UTC day, one day early for 00:00-05:30 IST publishes. findings.title: Letters reading page renders the letter's date in server UTC — and disagrees with the feed card, which formats the same timestamp in the browser
findings.expected: A letter posted at 11:50pm-plus IST (00:00-05:30 IST window) shows the IST date, and the same letter shows the same date everywhere it appears.
findings.actual: The reading page is a server component: the header meta formats createdAt inline with toLocaleDateString("en-GB") and the image caption uses formatDisplayDate() — both without timeZone, so both print the UTC day (one earlier for the 00:00-05:30 IST window). Meanwhile the feed's letter card runs post-card.tsx in the browser AFTER a client-side fetch (PostFeed loads via useEffect → loadPosts, no SSR of post data), so formatDisplayDate there uses the member's IST — the SAME letter can carry different dates on the feed card versus its own reading page. bugs.md item 6 tracks this class for the letters INDEX only; the reading page is a distinct, untracked surface.
findings.evidence: letters/[id]/page.tsx:165-169 (server component): `new Date(letter.createdAt).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" })`; :188: `date={formatDisplayDate(letter.createdAt)}`. utils.ts:151-157: `export function formatDisplayDate(date: Date | string): string { return new Date(date).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "short", year: "numeric" }) }` — no timeZone. Client-side contrast: post-feed.tsx loads posts in `useEffect` (line 92+, calling the loadPosts action), so post-card.tsx:108 `date: formatDisplayDate(post.createdAt)` executes only in the browser (IST).
findings.fixDirection: Add `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"` to formatDisplayDate in utils.ts (one line fixes the caption, the letters index tracked in bugs.md, admin surfaces, and keeps client callers consistent — IST is right for members abroad too, since the site's day is the Valley's day), and to the inline long-form call in letters/[id]/page.tsx:165.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test beside the existing utils tests (node --test, TZ=UTC): formatDisplayDate(new Date('2026-08-21T19:30:00Z')) === '22 Aug 2026'.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (TZ=UTC node one-liner shows the off-by-one for any 18:30-24:00 UTC instant).

findings.title: Collection photo detail page renders the uploader date in server UTC while the grid renders it in the browser — same photo, two dates
findings.expected: A photo uploaded 00:00-05:30 IST shows its IST date, identically on the collection grid and the photo's own page.
findings.actual: collection/[id]/page.tsx is a server component formatting `photo.createdAt` with toLocaleDateString("en-GB") and no timeZone → UTC day (one early in the window). The grid (collection-client.tsx) starts with `useState<PhotoData[]>([])` and fetches in useEffect, so its formatDisplayDate call runs only in the browser (IST) → correct. The two surfaces disagree for window uploads.
findings.evidence: collection/[id]/page.tsx:145-149: `meta={new Date(photo.createdAt).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "short", year: "numeric" })}` in a file with no "use client". collection-client.tsx:91 `const [photos, setPhotos] = useState<PhotoData[]>([]);` + :146 useEffect fetch → :77 `date: formatDisplayDate(p.createdAt)` executes client-side only.

findings.expected: The owner reads these pages as fact; a payment made 1:00am IST on the 22nd should read the 22nd.

findings.evidence: admin/support/page.tsx:222: `formatDisplayDate(new Date(r.paidAt ?? r.createdAt))`; admin/catchups/page.tsx:136-138: `? \`Sent ${formatDisplayDate(round.publishedAt)}\` : due ? \`${isStuck ? "Was due" : "Due"} ${formatDisplayDate(due)}\``; utils.ts:21-25 fallback: `return date.toLocaleDateString("en-IN", { day: "numeric", month: "short", year: "numeric" })` — no timeZone in either helper; all listed pages are server components.

findings.title: Member messages surfaces show UTC dates for messages older than 4 weeks (formatTimeAgo fallback, server-rendered)

Member-facing, narrow.

findings.title: Admin aggregates bucket days and months at UTC boundaries (5:30 IST shift): 'Given this month', distinct-day loyalty, daysActive, returning, growth-by-month
findings.expected: Day- and month-bucketed admin numbers count the community's IST days/months.
findings.actual: All boundaries are UTC: monthStart (setDate(1); setHours(0,0,0,0) under a UTC process) = the 1st at 05:30 IST, so payments made 00:00-05:30 IST on the 1st count into the previous month's 'Given this month'; date_trunc('day', ...) on naive-UTC timestamps splits days at 05:30 IST for the loyalty leaderboard (distinct days), MemberRow.daysActive, and the 'returning' count (a member visiting 11pm and 6am IST — one IST night — counts as two 'days'; one visiting 4am and 11pm IST — two IST days — counts as one); loadGrowth buckets joins with date_trunc('month') at UTC. Systematic 5.5-hour skew on admin-only aggregates; individually small, collectively the page's day-numbers are all shifted the same way.
findings.evidence: admin/page.tsx:63-65: `const monthStart = new Date(now); monthStart.setDate(1); monthStart.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);` then :77 `paidAt: { gte: monthStart }`. admin-analytics.ts:622 `count(DISTINCT date_trunc('day', v."startedAt"))`; :443 `HAVING count(DISTINCT date_trunc('day', "startedAt")) > 1`; :956 `count(DISTINCT date_trunc('day', "startedAt")) days`; :810-815 `date_trunc('month', "createdAt")`. All operate on naive columns holding UTC wall time.
findings.fixDirection: In SQL, use `date_trunc('day', ("startedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')` (same double-conversion as the rhythm fix; one helper SQL fragment shared across the file). In JS, compute monthStart as the IST month boundary (e.g. build from the Asia/Kolkata Y-M via Intl, or add the 5:30 offset explicitly with a comment).
findings.gateOrTest: The rhythm-heatmap SQL assertion generalizes; alternatively a fix-session read-only query comparing bucket counts under both expressions for a known window.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only SQL: for one userId, `SELECT count(DISTINCT date_trunc('day', "startedAt")), count(DISTINCT date_trunc('day', ("startedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')) FROM "Visit" WHERE ...` — values diverge whenever visits straddle 05:30 IST.

findings.title: Deletion-scheduled email names a purge date formatted in UTC — one day earlier than the IST purge day for late-night requests
findings.expected: The account-deletion confirmation names the IST calendar day on which the 60-day grace window ends.
findings.actual: A server action formats purgeAt (= now + 60d, an instant) with toLocaleDateString("en-GB") and no timeZone. For requests made 00:00-05:30 IST, purgeAt's UTC day is one before its IST day, so the email promises e.g. "20 October" for a purge whose instant is 01:00 IST on the 21st. Direction is conservative (signing in before the stated date always cancels in time), so severity is Low, but the date in a legally-flavoured email is simply wrong for the member's calendar. (Same-pattern cosmetic: the audit strings at settings/actions.ts:333 and retention.ts:132 record the UTC day via toISOString().slice(0,10).)
findings.evidence: settings/actions.ts:315: `const purgeAt = new Date(Date.now() + DELETION_GRACE_DAYS * 86_400_000);` and :344-348: `purgeDate: purgeAt.toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" })` — executed inside the server action (UTC), then baked into the queued email payload (email-queue.ts:395 passes it straight to deletionScheduledTemplate).
findings.fixDirection: Add `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"` to this toLocaleDateString call (the payload is a prerendered string, so it must be fixed at enqueue time, not render time).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on a small extracted formatPurgeDate helper with TZ=UTC pinning an 18:30-24:00 UTC instant to the next-day IST date.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (the write path sends real mail; do not exercise live).

findings.title: Feed time filter ('today'/'week'/'month'/'year') computes boundaries in server UTC — latent, since the filter UI is currently unreachable
findings.expected: "Today" means since IST midnight; "This week/month/year" start at IST boundaries.
findings.actual: getTimeFilterDate builds boundaries from server-local (UTC) date parts: "today" = since 05:30 IST (posts from 00:00-05:30 IST missing), and for a member browsing 00:00-05:30 IST the server's date is still yesterday, so "today" returns since 05:30 IST of the PREVIOUS day — nearly a full extra day labelled today. Week starts Sunday-at-UTC, month/year likewise. Mitigating fact making this latent: the only consumer of PostFeed's filter UI is the feed page, which passes showControls={false} (feed/page.tsx:79), and the select at post-feed.tsx:236 renders only under showControls — so no member can currently reach it. But loadPosts is a public server action that honours timeFilter for any caller, and re-surfacing the control re-exposes the bug untouched.
findings.evidence: feed/actions.ts:747-759: `case "today": return new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate()); case "week": { const d = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate()); d.setDate(d.getDate() - d.getDay()); ... case "month": return new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), 1);` — all server-local constructors in a "use server" actions file running UTC.
findings.fixDirection: Compute the boundaries in IST: derive the IST Y/M/D (e.g. via Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone Asia/Kolkata or by adding 330 minutes before taking date parts, with a comment), then build the UTC instant of that IST midnight (istMidnightUtc = Date.UTC(y, m, d) - 5.5h). Do it now while the code is latent, so the control can return safely.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on an extracted pure getTimeFilterDate(now) with fixed inputs: now = 2026-08-21T20:00:00Z (01:30 IST Aug 22) must yield today-boundary 2026-08-21T18:30:00Z, not 2026-08-21T00:00:00Z.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (UI unreachable; the action would need a hand-rolled invocation).

findings.title: SSR'd client components format dates without a hydration guard — recoverable hydration errors and a wrong-date/wrong-format flash
findings.expected: Client components whose date props arrive server-side render identical text on the SSR pass and at hydration — the codebase already knows this rule: verify-email-banner.tsx:113-126 routes its time label through useSyncExternalStore with an empty server snapshot precisely because "SSR said '5:30 am' where a 24-hour browser said '5:30', and React threw a hydration mismatch" (caught live 2026-08-13).
findings.actual: Several "use client" components receiving server-fetched data still format during SSR with browser-dependent output. Strongest: ExtendDeadlineCard (rendered inside CatchupHomeShell, a client shell fed by the server page) formats with locale `undefined` — Node's default (en-US) on the server vs the member's own locale in the browser, so "Replies close Tuesday, Aug 12" vs "Tuesday 12 Aug" mismatches for every non-en-US Keeper on every render; plus the TZ window shifts the weekday/day for 18:30-24:00 UTC deadlines. ArchiveShelf/ConsolePublished (en-IN) and DraftsStrip (en-GB, letters page) mismatch for timestamps in the 18:30-24:00 UTC window; the admin client lists (mail-rows, content-list, person-detail, report-list) same. React recovers by patching the text, so the end state is correct, but each occurrence logs a hydration error (Sentry noise) with a brief wrong-value flash. The main feed, comments, notification bell and collection grid are NOT affected — they fetch client-side.
findings.evidence: extend-deadline-card.tsx:48-52: `return at.toLocaleDateString(undefined, { weekday: "long", day: "numeric", month: "short" });` in a "use client" file; catchup-home-shell.tsx is "use client" and is rendered by the server page app/(main)/catchups/[catchupId]/page.tsx, so the SSR pass executes this with Node's locale and UTC. archive-shelf.tsx:21: `new Date(iso).toLocaleDateString("en-IN", { day: "numeric", month: "short", year: "numeric" })`; drafts-strip.tsx:97 (imported by the server page letters/page.tsx): `new Date(d.updatedAt).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", {...})` — none guarded. Contrast the in-repo precedent: verify-email-banner.tsx:122-126 `useSyncExternalStore(subscribeNever, () => (sendingAtIso ? sendTimeLabel(sendingAtIso) : ""), () => "")`.
findings.fixDirection: Pin every such call to an explicit locale AND timeZone "Asia/Kolkata" (making server and client output byte-identical — the cheap fix, right for date-only strings), or for genuinely browser-local values copy the verify-banner useSyncExternalStore pattern. Fix extend-deadline-card's `undefined` locale first; it mismatches independent of the TZ window.
findings.gateOrTest: e2e: the visual/e2e suite can assert zero hydration-error console messages on /catchups/[id] and /letters for a keeper fixture; unit: pinned-locale formatter output test.
findings.reproPlan: Live-provable read-only: open a Catch-up home as a Keeper (dev login) in chrome-devtools with a non-en-US browser locale and read list_console_messages for the hydration error.

findings.title: Zod year ceilings snapshot getFullYear() at module load in server TZ — rejects the new year for 5.5 IST hours (longer on a warm lambda)
findings.expected: On 1 January (IST), a member can enter the new year where the form allows the current year — e.g. the collection photo's year field, or yearLeft for schooling.
findings.actual: Two stacked staleness sources: (1) `new Date().getFullYear()` runs on the server in UTC, which is still last year until 05:30 IST on 1 Jan, so "That year hasn't happened yet" (validators.ts:188) rejects the year that has already begun in India; (2) the expressions sit in module-scope schema definitions, evaluated once per process — a warm serverless instance loaded in December keeps last year's ceiling until recycled, extending the window past 05:30. Fields with +1/+7 slack (yearLeft, batchYear) only pinch at their own edges; the exact-current-year ceilings (yearJoined, taughtFrom/Until at :105-109, the photo year at :188) hit every New Year's night.
findings.evidence: validators.ts:188: `.max(new Date().getFullYear(), "That year hasn't happened yet")` — module scope, no timeZone, evaluated at import. Same pattern :22-23, :104-109. These schemas validate server actions, so the server's clock and module lifetime govern, not the member's.
findings.fixDirection: Make the ceiling request-time and IST: replace the static .max() with a .refine() (or superRefine) that computes the current IST year per validation call — e.g. Number(new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en', { timeZone: 'Asia/Kolkata', year: 'numeric' }).format(new Date())).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on the extracted currentIstYear() helper: for a mocked instant 2026-12-31T19:00:00Z it must return 2027.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (needs a New Year boundary or clock mock).

findings.title: Nightly PostHog snapshot queries a UTC day 3 hours before it ends — every day's posthog.* metrics permanently undercount
findings.expected: MetricSnapshot's posthog.events/people/pageviews for day N cover all of day N.
findings.actual: The cron fires at 21:00 UTC ('0 21 * * *' = 02:30 IST); DAY resolves to the current UTC day; the HogQL filter `toDate(timestamp) = toDate(DAY)` therefore counts only 00:00-21:00 UTC of a day with 3 hours left. Events from 21:00-24:00 UTC (02:30-05:30 IST — small for this community, but nonzero) are never attributed to any day: the next night's run queries the NEXT date, and the day/source/metric upsert key means no later run revisits it. The db.* metrics are unaffected (they are totals-as-of, and 02:30 IST is a sensible IST-day close); this is specific to the range-queried PostHog source.
findings.evidence: snapshot.yml:15-16: `schedule: - cron: '0 21 * * *'`. snapshot.mjs:28: `const DAY = args.includes("--day") ? ... : startOfUtcToday();` and :199-203: `SELECT count() AS events, ... FROM events WHERE toDate(timestamp) = toDate('${iso}')` where iso = DAY. Nothing ever re-runs a finished day.
findings.fixDirection: Query yesterday for PostHog: use `daysAgo(1)` as the PostHog date (the just-finished UTC day) while leaving the db totals stamped on DAY — or simplest, have collectPostHog subtract one day from iso and store under that same shifted day key for posthog.* metrics.
findings.gateOrTest: A --dry run assertion in the script (log which date window each source covered) plus a comment; hard to unit-test beyond pinning the date arithmetic of daysAgo(1).
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: workflow_dispatch snapshot.mjs --dry (no writes) and inspect the logged PostHog date vs run time; or compare a stored posthog.events row against PostHog's own UI number for the same date.
